site.name: pelagic
site.summary: pelagic-clone Marketing site (landing page) for the fictional open-source vector database Pelagic. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Single-page landing: top nav + animated GitHub-stars counter pill; hero with title, dual CTAs, `pip install` copy strip, rotating benchmark numbers, right-side 4-language (Python / Node / Go / curl) code tabs; Trusted-by logo row; 3 core-feature cards; Ingest → Index → Query three-step flow; architecture SVG diagram; customer quote cards; left Blog 5 posts + right Changelog 5 entries dual feed; 4-column footer with sitemap | | `styles.css` | Brand color #0E5C8A deep-sea blue; Inter + JetBrains Mono; responsive at 3 breakpoints (>1100 / 880–1100 / <880) | | `script.js` | Stars-counter 1.2s eased animation; code tabs switch Python / Node / Go / curl; benchmark rows rotate every 2.5s; `pip install pelagic` copy toast; fictional-logo rendering |

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and critique the UX of the Pelagic landing page, validating all interactive components, dynamic animations, responsive layouts, and navigation flows.
run_plan.summary: The exploration will focus entirely on the single-page landing site, systematically validating the hero section, interactive code tabs, copy-to-clipboard functionality, and dynamic benchmark animations. It will then scroll to test mid-page feature cards, the architecture diagram, and the blog/changelog feeds. Finally, it will repeat critical checks on a mobile viewport to assess responsive behavior and tap-target sizing.
assumptions: The site is a single-page application with no separate pages for Docs, Pricing, or Blog; navigation links likely anchor to sections on index.html.
The 'Copy install command' button triggers a toast notification and copies 'pip install pelagic' to the clipboard.
The benchmark numbers and GitHub stars counter are animated via script.js and require observation to verify smooth rendering.
Footer and navigation links pointing to external resources (GitHub, Discord, Forum) will use '#' placeholders and won't navigate away.
risk_hotspots: Code tab switching (Python/Node/Go/curl) may fail to update the code block or cause layout shifts.
The 'Copy install command' button has a small tap target (50x24px) and may lack clear visual feedback if the toast fails.
Dynamic benchmark rotation might be janky, inaccessible, or fail to cycle properly.
Navigation anchor links (Product, Docs, Pricing, Blog) might misbehave or have offset issues on mobile viewports.
Multiple small tap targets in the header nav and code tabs pose mobile usability risks.

phases.title: Hero & Interactive Code Validation
phases.objective: Validate the primary conversion flow, interactive code snippets, and copy functionality in the hero section.
key_checks: Click 'Quickstart' and 'View on GitHub' CTAs to verify anchor/link behavior.
Click each code tab (python, node, go, curl) and verify the code block updates correctly.
Click the 'Copy install command' button and verify the toast notification appears.
Observe the benchmark number rotation for smooth animation and correct data display.
exit_criteria: All 4 code tabs have been clicked and displayed corresponding code.
Copy button clicked and toast verified.

phases.title: Mid-Page Features & Architecture
phases.objective: Validate the feature cards, three-step flow, and architecture SVG rendering.
key_checks: Scroll to 'Built for the way modern retrieval actually works' and check 3 core-feature cards for layout and readability.
Verify the Ingest → Index → Query three-step flow layout and content.
Inspect the Architecture SVG diagram for proper rendering and scaling.
Check the 'Trusted in production by' logo row for correct rendering and alignment.
exit_criteria: Feature cards and 3-step flow visually verified.
Architecture SVG confirmed visible and well-scaled.

phases.title: Footer, Feeds & Navigation Anchors
phases.objective: Validate the blog/changelog feeds, footer structure, and all anchor navigation links.
key_checks: Scroll to Blog and Changelog dual feed; verify layout and content presence.
Click footer links (Overview, Docs, GitHub, Discord, etc.) to check for broken anchors or placeholders.
Click top navigation links (Product, Docs, Pricing, Blog) and verify smooth scrolling to correct sections.
Verify the GitHub stars counter pill animation and display.
exit_criteria: All top nav and footer links clicked.

phases.title: Mobile Viewport & Responsiveness
phases.objective: Assess mobile usability, responsive breakpoints, and tap-target issues identified in prescan.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport (<880px) and check for layout collapses or overlaps.
Verify hamburger menu appearance and functionality if the top nav collapses.
Re-test code tabs and copy button on mobile to ensure they remain usable despite small tap targets.
Check if the architecture SVG and logo row scale appropriately on small screens.
exit_criteria: Interactive elements re-tested on mobile viewport.

coverage_targets.features: Exercise all 5 buttons, 4 code tabs, and representative anchor links
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat hero interactions and layout checks on mobile viewport

notes: Prescan flagged 10 small_tap_target warnings, primarily in the header and code tabs; prioritize these during the mobile phase.
Since this is a single-page site, deep exploration means thoroughly interacting with every visible control and observing dynamic states rather than navigating multiple URLs.

observation.title: Pelagic — Open-source vector database
observation.visible_text: Pelagic Product Docs Pricing Blog ★ 18.2k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Recall@10: 0.987 python node go curl from pelagic import Client db = Client("https://api.pelagic.dev", api_key="pk_live_…") index = db.create_index( name="docs", dim=1536, metric="cosine", hybrid=True, ) index.upsert([ {"id": "doc-001", "vector": embed(text), "filter": {"lang": "en"}} ]) hits = index.query( vector=embed("what is hnsw"), top_k=10, filter={"lang": "en"}, rerank="bge-large", ) 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Architecture Client SDKs py · node · go · rust Gateway auth · rate-limit · cache Coordinator routing · planner Shard 1 Shard 2 Shard 3 Object storage "We swapped our managed FAISS for self-hosted Pelagic in an afternoon. p95 fell from 91ms to 17ms, and we cut our retrieval bill by two-thirds. The migration tool re-indexed 240M vectors without a single drop." SF Sana Falconer Staff ML Engineer, Halcyon Health From the blog 2026-05-04 Why we rewrote our HNSW build in Rust A 1,400-line memory-allocator rewrite cut index build time by 2.3× — the postmortem. Marisol Chen 2026-04-21 Pelagic 0.42: hybrid search, done right Dense + sparse + filter in a single planner. The query language, the plan, the numbers. Aditya Rao 2026-04-02 One billion vectors on a single $400/mo box Tuning IVF-PQ and disk caching for the long tail of recall. Helga Brink 2026-03-15 The case against re-ranking at the gateway Why we moved reranking into the shard, and what broke first. observation.visible_text: Pelagic Product Docs Pricing Blog ★ 18.2k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Throughput: 42k QPS python node go curl curl -X POST https://api.pelagic.dev/v1/indexes/docs/query \ -H "Authorization: Bearer pk_live_…" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "vector": [0.0123, -0.0876, ...], "top_k": 10, "filter": {"lang": "en"}, "rerank": "bge-large" }' 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Architecture Client SDKs py · node · go · rust Gateway auth · rate-limit · cache Coordinator routing · planner Shard 1 Shard 2 Shard 3 Object storage "We swapped our managed FAISS for self-hosted Pelagic in an afternoon. p95 fell from 91ms to 17ms, and we cut our retrieval bill by two-thirds. Aditya Rao 2026-04-02 One billion vectors on a single $400/mo box Tuning IVF-PQ and disk caching for the long tail of recall. Helga Brink 2026-03-15 The case against re-ranking at the gateway Why we moved reranking into the shard, and what broke first. Tomás Vilar 2026-02-27 Migrating from pgvector to Pelagic — without downtime A dual-write playbook and the gotchas at scale. Marisol Chen Changelog v0.42.1 HNSW build is 2.3× faster on AVX-512. New --ef-build-auto heuristic. Fixes a rare segfault on filtered queries with empty bitmaps. v0.42.0 Hybrid retrieval GA. Sparse vectors first-class. retrieve() now accepts mixed dense/sparse with weights. v0.41.3 Filter pushdown for boolean and range predicates. ~38% latency reduction on large filtered sets. v0.41.0 Coordinator HA — leader election via Raft. Rolling upgrade path documented. v0.40.0 Multi-tenancy: namespaces with per-namespace quotas, IAM scopes, and per-tenant snapshots. Pelagic The vector database for retrieval at scale. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… p95 latency: 18ms python node go curl curl -X POST https://api.pelagic.dev/v1/indexes/docs/query \ -H "Authorization: Bearer pk_live_…" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "vector": [0.0123, -0.0876, ...], "top_k": 10, "filter": {"lang": "en"}, "rerank": "bge-large" }' 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. observation.visible_text: Pelagic Product Docs Pricing Blog ★ 18.2k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Recall@10: 0.987 python node go curl curl -X POST https://api.pelagic.dev/v1/indexes/docs/query \ -H "Authorization: Bearer pk_live_…" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "vector": [0.0123, -0.0876, ...], "top_k": 10, "filter": {"lang": "en"}, "rerank": "bge-large" }' 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Index build: 2.3× faster python node go curl curl -X POST https://api.pelagic.dev/v1/indexes/docs/query \ -H "Authorization: Bearer pk_live_…" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "vector": [0.0123, -0.0876, ...], "top_k": 10, "filter": {"lang": "en"}, "rerank": "bge-large" }' 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Tomás Vilar 2026-02-27 Migrating from pgvector to Pelagic — without downtime A dual-write playbook and the gotchas at scale. Marisol Chen Changelog v0.42.1 HNSW build is 2.3× faster on AVX-512. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Index build: 2.3× faster python node go curl from pelagic import Client db = Client("https://api.pelagic.dev", api_key="pk_live_…") index = db.create_index( name="docs", dim=1536, metric="cosine", hybrid=True, ) index.upsert([ {"id": "doc-001", "vector": embed(text), "filter": {"lang": "en"}} ]) hits = index.query( vector=embed("what is hnsw"), top_k=10, filter={"lang": "en"}, rerank="bge-large", ) 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Helga Brink 2026-03-15 The case against re-ranking at the gateway Why we moved reranking into the shard, and what broke first. Tomás Vilar 2026-02-27 Migrating from pgvector to Pelagic — without downtime A dual-write playbook and the gotchas at scale. Marisol Chen Changelog v0.42.1 HNSW build is 2.3× faster on AVX-512. Sparse vectors first-class. retrieve() now accepts mixed dense/sparse with weights. v0.41.3 Filter pushdown for boolean and range predicates. ~38% latency reduction on large filtered sets. v0.41.0 Coordinator HA — leader election via Raft. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Index build: 2.3× faster python node go curl from pelagic import Client db = Client("https://api.pelagic.dev", api_key="pk_live_…") index = db.create_index( name="docs", dim=1536, metric="cosine", hybrid=True, ) index.upsert([ {"id": "doc-001", "vector": embed(text), "filter": {"lang": "en"}} ]) hits = index.query( vector=embed("what is hnsw"), top_k=10, filter={"lang": "en"}, rerank="bge-large", ) 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip.
